match.reason: The closest bank point covers physical and chemical barriers but says nothing about microbiological barriers such as normal bacteria, so adding that would be new content rather than a small adjustment, and a wrong match would teach the wrong thing.

draft.title: Physical, chemical and microbiological barriers
card: a barrier that blocks entry. Intact skin is a tough layer pathogens cannot easily cross. Mucus in the airways traps them, and cilia (tiny hairs) sweep it out.
a substance that kills or harms pathogens. Stomach acid destroys many swallowed microbes. Lysozyme, an enzyme in tears and saliva, breaks down bacterial cell walls.
normal bacteria living on the skin and in the gut. They use up food and space, so harmful microbes struggle to settle.
These barriers work first and work on any pathogen. They stop most pathogens getting in, but a cut or a damaged surface can let some through.
draft.remember: Barriers stop entry by blocking, by harming, or by crowding out pathogens.

a.q: Which of these is a chemical barrier against pathogens?
opts: Lysozyme in tears breaking down bacterial cell walls
Cilia sweeping mucus out of the airways
Skin cells forming a tough outer layer
Normal gut bacteria competing for food and space
a.why: Lysozyme is an enzyme that harms bacteria, so it is a chemical barrier. Cilia and skin block or remove pathogens, and gut bacteria crowd them out, so they are not chemical.
a.clue: Which one is a substance that damages the pathogen?

b.q: After a course of antibiotics, Sam gets a fungal infection in his gut. Which barrier has most likely been weakened?
opts: The microbiological barrier of normal gut bacteria
The physical barrier of skin on his body
The chemical barrier of lysozyme in his tears
The physical barrier of mucus in his airways
b.why: Antibiotics can kill the normal bacteria in the gut. With fewer of them using up food and space, a harmful fungus can settle more easily. The other barriers are not in the gut or are not affected by antibiotics in this way.
b.clue: Which barrier is made of living microbes that antibiotics can kill?

a.best: Lysozyme in tears breaking down bacterial cell walls

b.best: The microbiological barrier of normal gut bacteria
